'''Yamuna Expressway''' is a 6-[[lane]] (expandable to 8), {{convert|165.5|km|mi|1|abbr=on}} long [[Controlled-access highway|access-controlled expressway in]] the Indian state of [[Uttar Pradesh]]. It is presently India's sixth longest expressway and connects [[Greater Noida]] with [[Agra]]. It was built to de-congest the older Delhi–Agra national highway [[National Highway 2 (India, old numbering)|(NH-2)]] or Mathura Road. The [[Noida–Greater Noida Expressway|Noida-Greater Noida Expressway]] feeds into the project.

Built by [[Jaypee Infratech|Jaypee Infratech Ltd (JIL)]] on a [[Build–operate–transfer|BOT (Build-Operate-Transfer)]] basis, the company has the rights to collect for a period of 36 years, starting from its Commercial Operations Date (COD) on August 9, 2012 until the agreement expires, after which the expressway will be transferred to the Yamuna Expressway Industrial Development Authority (YEIDA). The Yamuna Expressway Industrial Development Authority (YEIDA) region is being developed over an area of approximately 25,000 hectares along the Yamuna Expressway in the state of Uttar Pradesh. The region includes the Noida International Airport at Jewar which is under development and is planned to be one of the largest airports in India.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Infrastructure Development – Yamuna Expressway Authority |url=https://www.yamunaexpresswayauthority.com/web/about-us/infrastructure/ |website=Yamuna Expressway Industrial Development Authority |access-date=2026-06-03}}</ref>


The [[Noida International Airport]] located in Jewar of the [[Gautam Buddha Nagar district|Gautam Buddha Nagar]] District also lies on the side of the expressway, with it acting as the main connection to multiple cities.

The expressway saw an investment {{INRConvert|12839|c|lk=on}} and was inaugurated on 9 August 2012 by then Chief Minister of UP [[Akhilesh Yadav]].<ref name="indiatimes1">{{cite news|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/delhi/Yamuna-Expressway-opens-one-way-toll-Rs-320-free-ride-till-Aug-15/articleshow/15419665.cms |title=Yamuna Expressway opens, one-way toll Rs 320, free ride till Aug 15|work=The Times of India|date=9 August 2012|agency=Times News Network|access-date=6 June 2018}}</ref><ref>{{cite news|url=http://www.thehindubusinessline.com/companies/article3721785.ece |title=Yamuna Expressway is ready, says Jaypee Infra |newspaper=Business Line|date=3 August 2012|access-date=6 June 2018}}</ref> A total of 13 service roads of about 168 [[km]] were built for local commuters to access the expressway.<ref>{{Cite web|url=http://www.roadtraffic-technology.com/projects/yamunaexpressway/|title=Yamuna Expressway – Verdict Traffic|access-date=12 June 2014|archive-date=19 July 2024|archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20240719083343/https://www.roadtraffic-technology.com/projects/yamunaexpressway/|url-status=dead}}</ref>{{Unreliable source?|reason=domain on WP:BLACKLIST|date=June 2016}}

==History==
After years of delays, construction was completed in May 2012,<ref>{{cite web |url=http://www.indianexpress.com/news/expressway-ready-jaypee-team-tells-up-officials/947199/ |title=Expressway ready: Jaypee team tells UP officials|date= 9 May 2012}}</ref> and the expressway was formally inaugurated on 9 August 2012,<ref name="indiatimes1" /> about two years behind its original target completion date.<ref>{{cite news| url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/delhi/Yamuna-e-way-opens-on-Aug-9/articleshow/15333395.cms | work=The Times of India | title=Yamuna e-way opens on Aug 9 | date=3 August 2012}}</ref>

==Yamuna Emergency Landing Field==
[[File:An Indian Air Force (IAF) Mirage -2000 lands at Yamuna Expressway, in Uttar Pradesh on May 20, 2015.jpg|thumb|IAF Mirage 2000 landing on the Yamuna Expressway]]
In a first for military aviation in India, the Indian Air Force on 21 May 2015 successfully landed a French [[Dassault Mirage 2000]] on the Yamuna Expressway near Raya village, Mathura.The mock drill was a practice run to evaluate the utility of highways for emergency landings by military aircraft.<ref>{{cite news| url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/india/IAF-successfully-test-lands-Mirage-on-Yamuna-e-way/articleshow/47378100.cms | work=The Times of India | title=IAF successfully test-lands Mirage on Yamuna e-way | date=22 May 2015}}</ref> 

== Characteristics ==
The Yamuna Expressway has SOS booths along the route besides a toll-free helpline. [[CCTV]] cameras are installed every {{convert|5|km|mi|abbr=on|sigfig=2}} along the expressway. There are mobile radars to monitor compliance with minimum and maximum speed limits; and one highway patrol every {{convert|25|km|mi|abbr=on|sigfig=2}}. The Expressway is expected to be used by over 100,000 vehicles every day, and reduce travel times between Greater Noida and Agra from four hours to one hour 40 minutes.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://yamunaexpresswayauthority.com/aboutus |title=About Us | Yamuna Expressway Industrial Development Authority |publisher=Yamunaexpresswayauthority.com |date=24 April 2001 |access-date=29 April 2012 |archive-date=21 April 2012 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20120421101947/http://www.yamunaexpresswayauthority.com/aboutus |url-status=dead }}</ref> There is a patrol station at Tappal, the halfway point on the expressway. Tappal {{convert|60|km|mi|abbr=on|sigfig=2}} from Noida Sec. 37 i.e. botanical garden.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://yamunaexpresswayauthority.com/features |title=Salient Features of the Yamuna Expressway Project (Yamuna Expressway Industrial Development Authority) |work=YEIDA |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20131207191714/http://yamunaexpresswayauthority.com/features |archive-date=7 December 2013 }}</ref> In 2025, the Yamuna Expressway successfully implemented all road safety measures recommended by an expert team from [[IIT Delhi]].<ref>{{Cite news |date=2025-03-31 |title=Yamuna Expressway meets safety norms advised by IIT-Delhi experts |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/lucknow/yamuna-expressway-meets-safety-norms-advised-by-iit-delhi-experts/articleshow/119799165.cms |access-date=2025-04-01 |work=The Times of India |issn=0971-8257}}</ref>

===Metro Rail connectivity===
Metro rail service from Pari Chowk to Yamuna Expressway Sector 18 and 20 will be added in the future, according to officials. 

==Development==
[[File:Yamuna Expressway Detailed Map.png|thumb|right|Yamuna Expressway within the state of Uttar Pradesh]]
[[File:Yamuna Expressway Toll Plaza Delhi Agra India.jpg|thumb|A toll plaza on Yamuna Expressway]]

The Expressway was developed by Yamuna Expressway Industrial Development Authority (YEIDA) in 3 phases and the contract was awarded to [[Jaypee Group|Jaypee Infratech Limited]]:
* Phase I: Expressway Stretch between [[Greater Noida]] & proposed Taj International Aviation Hub (near village Jewar on the southern tip of Dist. Gautam Budh Nagar).
* Phase II: Expressway Stretch between proposed Taj International Aviation Hub and an intermediate destination between proposed Taj International Aviation Hub & [[Agra]].
* Phase III: Expressway Stretch between intermediate destination & [[Agra]].

'''Speed Limit'''
The speed limit on the expressway is {{convert|100|km/h|mph|sigfig=2|abbr=on}} for vehicles. The right most lane on the expressway is reserved for overtaking only.<ref>{{cite news|title=Yamuna Expressway: From Dec, zoon to Agra at 120 km/h|work=The Times of India|date=9 November 2011|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/noida/From-Dec-zoom-to-Agra-at-100kmph/articleshow/10660483.cms}}</ref> Heavy vehicles are limited to a maximum speed of 60 kilometers per hour.<ref name=":0" />

'''Upcoming Residential Project'''
Yamuna Expressway has become most preferred for Builders and developers. Many reputed builders are bringing residential projects at Yamuna Expressway. To inject new life into the real estate market, Yamuna Expressway Industrial Development Authority has come up with lucrative affordable housing projects.<ref>{{cite news|title=YEIDA launches 5 schemes|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/noida/YEIDA-launches-5-schemes/articleshow/52560822.cms|date=2 June 2016}}</ref> Under the new subvention scheme YEIDA has launched 200 small ticket size apartments and 80 large size residential flats.

'''Agra–Lucknow connectivity'''
A {{convert|302|km|mi|abbr=on|sigfig=3}} [[Agra–Lucknow Expressway]] Project is completed with estimated budget of {{INR}} 15,000 crore extends YEA to [[Lucknow]] enabling fast transit.
Agra–Lucknow Expressway will extend to the proposed Sanjay Khan project of a theme park of seven cities. Yamuna Expressway linked to Agra-Lucknow Expressway through Agra Inner Ring Road Expressway {{convert|11.9|km|mi|abbr=on|sigfig=3}} which also shortens the distance and avoid the heavy traffic of Agra, tourists can directly reach Taj Mahal. In March 2025, the Indian government approved the project to connect the Yamuna Expressway with the Delhi-Agra Highway.<ref>{{Cite web |title=Rs 1,645 cr project to connect Yamuna Expressway with Delhi-Agra Highway approved |url=https://www.ptinews.com/story/national/rs-1-645-cr-project-to-connect-yamuna-expressway-with-delhi-agra-highway-approved/2425575 |access-date=2025-04-03 |website=PTI News}}</ref><ref>{{Cite web |last=Negi |first=Priyanka |title=Good News! Govt Approves Rs 1,645 Crore Project To Link Yamuna Expressway With Delhi-Agra Highway, Boosting Mathura-Vrindavan Connectivity |url=https://news24online.com/india/good-news-govt-approves-rs-1645-crore-project-to-link-yamuna-expressway-with-delhi-agra-highway-boosting-mathura-vrindavan-connectivity/520177/ |access-date=2025-04-03 |website=News24 |language=en}}</ref>

== Goals ==
The goals of the expressway are as follows:

# To establish a high-speed corridor for efficient travel time reduction.
# To link key [[Built-up area (Highway Code)|built-up area]] and commercial zones situated on the eastern side of the Yamuna River.
# To foster development in the surrounding areas.
# To alleviate [[traffic congestion]] on NH-2, which passes through densely populated cities like '''[[Faridabad]]''', Ballabgarh, and [[Palwal]].
# To, combined with NH-2 and NH-91, create an extensive road network, promoting comprehensive development.
# Facilitate swift transportation of essential supplies and aid to affected regions during emergencies such as flooding along the Yamuna River.<ref>{{Cite news |date=2012-08-10 |title=Yamuna Expressway - Everything You Need to Know |url=https://www.ondrive.in/yamuna-expressway.html |access-date=2024-04-05 |work=OnDrive |language=en-US}}</ref>

== Features ==
The Yamuna Expressway is one of India's lengthiest access-controlled [[concrete]] [[Controlled-access highway|expressway]].

Emergency medical services, including ambulances and hospital tie-ups, are available for accidents and medical emergencies.

The expressway is equipped with [[closed-circuit television]] surveillance, which is used to monitor vehicle's speeds.

Authorities plan to install [[fuelling station]]s, food courts, ATMs, and public restrooms along the expressway.<ref name=":0">{{Cite web |last=Hussain |first=Raza Rahil |date=2012-08-10 |title=Yamuna Expressway - Everything You Need to Know |url=https://www.ondrive.in/yamuna-expressway.html |access-date=2024-04-05 |language=en-US}}</ref>

==Toll rates==
Toll are charged at three points along the expressway. Cars are charged {{INR}}{{convert|2.65|km|mi|abbr=on|sigfig=3|disp=preunit|/|/}} and mini-buses {{INR}}{{convert|3.85|km|mi|abbr=on|sigfig=3|disp=preunit|/|/}}. Buses and Trucks are charged {{INR}}{{convert|7.85|km|mi|abbr=on|sigfig=3|disp=preunit|/|/}}. Heavy vehicles are charged {{INR}}{{convert|11.94|km|mi|abbr=on|sigfig=4|disp=preunit|/|/}}.<ref>{{cite news|title=Toll rates for Yamuna expressway|url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/lucknow/Yamuna-Expressway-UP-government-finally-notifies-toll-rates/articleshow/15413358.cms|access-date=9 August 2012|newspaper=The Times of India}}</ref>

There are 16 [[toll (fee)|toll]] plazas on each side of the [[Controlled-access highway|expressway]].<ref name=":0" />

==Status updates==
* '''Apr 2001:''' A 6-lane wide expressway is conceived between [[Greater Noida]] and [[Agra]] by the then Chief Minister of [[Uttar Pradesh]] (Oct 2000-Mar 2002) [[Rajnath Singh]]. Taj Expressway Authority (TEA), a statutory body constituted on 20 April 2001.<ref>{{cite web |url=http://yamunaexpresswayauthority.com/yep.html |title=About Yamuna Expressway project |work=YEIDA |access-date=23 August 2021 |archive-date=28 November 2021 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20211128181423/http://yamunaexpresswayauthority.com/yep.html |url-status=dead }}</ref>
* '''Feb 2003:''' Concession Agreement between TEA and Jaypee Infratech Ltd ([[Jaypee Group]]) as the concessionaire was executed on 7 February 2003.
* '''Sep 2007:''' Land acquisition began by the Government of UP, led by the then Chief Minister (May 2007-Mar 2012) [[Mayawati]].
* '''Jan 2008:''' Construction work started by Jaypee Infratech Ltd. 
* '''July 2008:''' Taj Expressway renamed as Yamuna Expressway with effect from 11 July 2008.
* '''May 2011:''' Protest started by farmers of [[2011 Land acquisition protests in Uttar Pradesh|Bhatta and Parsaul]] villages near [[Dankaur]] in Gautam Buddha Nagar district. 
* '''Aug 2012:''' Yamuna Expressway is inaugurated by the then Chief Minister of Uttar Pradesh (Mar 2012-Mar 2017), [[Akhilesh Yadav]] on 9 August 2012.
* '''Jun 2021:''' [[Electronic toll collection]] has been started on 15 June 2021 by using [[FASTag]] RFID on vehicles.<ref>{{cite web |url=https://timesofindia.indiatimes.com/city/noida/fastag-on-yamuna-e-way-from-june-15/articleshow/83129208.cms |title=FASTag on Yamuna Expressway from 15 June |work=The Times of India |date=1 June 2021 }}</ref><ref>{{cite web |url=https://zeenews.india.com/automobile/bye-bye-long-queues-at-toll-plaza-fastag-on-yamuna-expressway-from-today-2369213.html |title=Bye-bye long queues at Toll Plaza! FASTag on Yamuna Expressway from today |work=Zee News |date=15 June 2021 }}</ref>
